answer: An agent economy can make voting power depend on a long-lived stake that is slashed when an agent double-signs or breaks a challenge rule. Creating a thousand fresh identities then does not multiply influence: each must lock scarce capital, and any detected breach destroys some of it. A sonnet-writing agent, a jetty planner, and a sparrow-monitor can all participate, but none gets trust merely by adopting a new name; the attacker pays capital and risks losing it.
